questions.answer: An AI workflow runs a model and tools through a fixed path that a developer defines, while an AI agent lets the model decide its own next steps and which tools to use until the task is done [1][2]. Workflows are more predictable and easier to test, which suits well-defined, repeatable tasks, whereas agents suit open-ended tasks where the steps can't be known in advance [1][2]. Agents usually make more model calls and take longer, so they tend to cost more [1][2]. Joe starts projects by scoping which one the job needs, and many end up as a workflow [6][8]. For a project, see [AI agent development](/services/ai-agent-development/) or reach out via the [contact page](/contact/).

questions.answer: Joe's site covers keyword research as a shift away from exact-match targeting toward user intent and conversational queries. Instead of targeting generic keywords, focus on the specific problems your audience wants to solve, and consider how they search on different platforms, not only Google [4]. Joe recommends identifying intent with tools that offer intent classification, looking at search volume patterns, SERP features, related keyword clusters and seasonal intent shifts [3]. He also suggests measuring results with frameworks that go beyond traditional ranking tracking [2].
